headline: Are there 3.5 million vegans in the UK?
rating_original: 3.5 million is almost certainly too high. The phrasing of the survey it’s based on means it could include people who were previously vegan but no longer are. The best available research we know of (from 2016) estimated 540,000 adults in Britain are vegan.
claim: The number of vegans in the UK has risen from half a million in 2016 to 3.5 million today.

headline: No evidence one million people legally moved to Britain in 2020/2021
rating_original: There is no data to prove this claim. It relies on information about immigration from the previous year, and makes assumptions about the number of people who would migrate to Britain over the course of 2020 and 2021—despite the pandemic.
claim: One million ‘legal migrants’ moved to Britain in 2020/21.

headline: One in seven parents don’t read to their 7-9 year-old for more than 15 minutes per week
rating_original: A survey found one in seven parents reads to their child aged seven to nine for less than 15 minutes per week. That doesn’t necessarily mean the child’s other parent isn’t reading to them as well.
claim: One in seven children aged seven to nine gets less than 15 minutes a week reading time with their parents.

headline: There is no EU police force being rolled out in the UK
rating_original: A photo shows an EU police force which is coming to the UK.
claim: The photo is of Peruvian police officers. There is no current policy for an EU police force.

headline: Stronger In "facts" leaflet: business
rating_original: HMRC figures from 2012 found almost 200,000 VAT-registered traders in the UK which traded goods with other EU member states. They said that the figure could be “significantly higher” if it included companies that traded in services.
claim: Over 200,000 UK businesses trade with the EU, helping them create jobs here in the UK.

headline: The EU has reduced roaming charges
rating_original: The EU has put a cap on the amount you can be charged for using your phone abroad, and prices have fallen. Networks won't generally be able to charge roaming fees at all from 2017.
claim: Roaming charges in Europe are lower because of the EU.

headline: Are a majority of youth knife offenders minority ethnic?
rating_original: In England and Wales 38% of knife possession offenders under 25s were non-white in 2017. It was two thirds in London.
claim: Two thirds of knife offenders under 25 were black or minority ethnic.

headline: No evidence Pfizer Covid-19 vaccine affects women’s fertility
rating_original: This claim has no basis. The spike protein on the Covid-19 virus and a protein that makes up the placenta have only a small amount in common, almost certainly not enough for the immune system to attack the placenta.
claim: The Covid-19 spike protein which the Pfizer vaccine causes an immune response against also trains the body to attack syncytin-1, a protein in the placenta, which could lead to infertility in women.

headline: You shouldn’t rely on a pregnancy test to tell you whether you have testicular cancer
rating_original: Some people with testicular cancer can get a positive result on a pregnancy test. But it is not a conclusive way of diagnosing yourself, and if you have any symptoms you should go to a doctor.
claim: If a man takes a pregnancy test and gets a positive result, it means he most likely has testicular cancer.

headline: Photo of Mike Tyson in ‘Plan-Demic’ t-shirt has been edited
rating_original: The photo has been altered to add a Plan-Demic logo.
claim: A photo of Mike Tyson shows him wearing a ‘Plan-Demic’ t-shirt.

headline: Labour's social housing record
rating_original: Mr Hunt's claim about the building of new social housing is factually accurate. However by using the figures to attack Labour's record it could be argued that he is glossing over the legacy of the previous Conservative government and a much longer trend of decline in social housing. Indeed the figures quoted show that the number of new homes being built each year fell by 72,850 under the Tories, but actually went up 2,220 under Labour. Nevertheless with waiting lists for social housing running at four million, the Tory frontbencher, is justified in questions over Labour's policy during the last 13 years.
claim: There is [sic] less social housing built in the last 13 years under Labour then there was under the previous Conservative Government

headline: Einstein didn’t say technology would create 'generation of idiots'
rating_original: There’s no record of him ever saying this. The first iterations of this quote appear to have been posted online in 2012.
claim: Albert Einstein said technology would one day “surpass our human interaction” and create “a generation of idiots”.

headline: There’s no easy way to compare benefit and tax fraud.
rating_original: This is out of date and newer estimates put this much higher at £2.3 billion for 2018/19.
claim: £1.2 billion is lost to benefit fraud.

headline: There’s no easy way to compare benefit and tax fraud.
rating_original: As of July 2018 the DWP employed 1,405 full-time equivalent specialists to investigate benefit fraud. Data from 2017 suggests another 2,000 or so full-time equivalent staff may be doing related work.
claim: The DWP employs the equivalent of 1,400 full time investigators

headline: There’s no easy way to compare benefit and tax fraud.
rating_original: In February 2018 HMRC employed around 26,000 people “tackling all forms of non-compliance in the tax system”
claim: HMRC employs 26,000 staff in tax compliance

headline: There’s no easy way to compare benefit and tax fraud.
rating_original: In 2017/18 HMRC estimated the ‘tax gap’ (money that should have been collected in taxes but wasn’t) at around £35 billion per year. Not all of this is due to fraud.
claim: £30 billion is lost to tax fraud.

headline: What is the advice on getting the Pfizer vaccine during pregnancy?
rating_original: It is true that the advice given by Pfizer and the advice given by health authorities differs. Pfizer said this is because it is not within the company’s remit to say there is sufficient clinical evidence to support pregnant women getting their Covid-19 vaccine safely. This decision is down to each individual country’s regulatory body.
claim: There is a discrepancy between information on Pfizer’s website and patient information leaflet and official government advice for pregnant women thinking about getting the Covid-19 vaccine.

headline: A Bill to change referendum rules came from one Lord, not the government
rating_original: Such a Bill has been proposed, but not by the Conservative party officially or by the government. It was put forward as a Private Members’ Bill by a Conservative member of the House of Lords and has not yet been debated.
claim: The Conservatives are planning to pass a Bill setting the threshold at which a referendum could pass. This would be 55% turnout, 60% in favour and two thirds of MPs agreeing to the referendum in the first place.

headline: Were 1.4 million stuck on out-of-work benefits under Labour?
rating_original: According to 2010 research by the Department for Work and Pensions, 1.4 million people were on out of work benefits in nine of the last ten years.
claim: Under the Labour party 1.4 million people spent most of the last decade on out-of-work benefits.

headline: Adult skills funding: what happened in the last Parliament?
rating_original: Analysis by membership body the Association of Colleges has shown that spending on core adult skills for those aged 19 and over fell by 35% between 2009/10 and 2015/16. The cut was about 41% once inflation is accounted for.
claim: Adult education has been cut by 35% during David Cameron’s time as Prime Minister.

headline: How did different constituencies vote in the 2016 EU referendum?
rating_original: Correct.
claim: 17.4 million people voted to leave and 16.1 million voted to remain in the EU referendum.

headline: How did different constituencies vote in the 2016 EU referendum?
rating_original: Best estimates show it was probably about 410 to 240.
claim: 406 constituencies voted to leave, 242 voted to remain in the EU referendum.

headline: How did different constituencies vote in the 2016 EU referendum?
rating_original: Best estimates are that 249 Conservative constituencies probably voted to leave, and 81 to remain (based on the 2015 general election seat distribution). For Labour it was 148 for leave, and 84 for remain.
claim: In the 2016 EU referendum, 148 Labour constituencies voted to leave, 84 to remain. 247 Conservative constituencies voted to leave, 80 to remain.

headline: How did different constituencies vote in the 2016 EU referendum?
rating_original: Correct.
claim: Nine regions voted to leave and three voted to remain in the EU referendum.

headline: How did different constituencies vote in the 2016 EU referendum?
rating_original: That’s pretty close to survey results of all the MPs just before the 2016 referendum. There has since been a general election and some MPs could have changed their view.
claim: 160 MPs are for leave and 486 are for remain.

headline: No evidence that smell of rosemary boosts memory by 75%
rating_original: There is no record of a 75% boost beyond a quote in the Daily Mail. One of the study’s authors has since said it was actually 7.5%.
claim: Scientists find sniffing rosemary can increase memory by 75%.

headline: Telegraph headline linking depression and social media isn't backed up by article
rating_original: The study referred to in the article does not show this, and the expert quoted in the article said that there could be a number of factors at play.
claim: By Votes 17.4 million Leave | 16.1 million Remain

headline: Videos of people giving their views on immigration are AI fakes
rating_original: These videos are fake. They contain SynthID watermarks and visual glitches which indicate they were generated using AI.
claim: Videos show members of the public talking about their views on immigration.

headline: Video of ‘Pallywood’ actor is actually from an Iraqi comedy skit
rating_original: That’s not what this video shows. The clip is from a comedy skit filmed in Iraq, and is unrelated to conflict in the Middle East.
claim: A clip showing a supposedly injured man hopping on the wrong leg is “Palestinian propaganda”.

headline: How many asylum seekers are being housed in Wales?
rating_original: This isn’t correct. The government publishes quarterly figures showing the number of asylum seekers being supported by each local authority in Wales. As of December 2025, 3,353 asylum seekers were being supported in Wales, most of whom were in Cardiff.
claim: We don’t know how many asylum seekers have been dispersed across Wales.

headline: David Lammy incorrectly claims Cyprus is ‘a NATO country’
rating_original: Incorrect. Cyprus is not a member of NATO.
claim: Cyprus is a NATO country.

headline: No evidence viral image of Epstein and Farage is real - here’s why experts say it’s probably AI
rating_original: There’s no evidence this is a real image. Reform UK has said it is “completely fake”, and experts say there are a number of details which suggest it was probably created with AI.
claim: A photo shows Jeffrey Epstein and Nigel Farage with their arms around each other.

headline: Unemployment has increased under Labour, but it hasn’t risen ‘every single month
rating_original: That’s not quite right. Both the number of people who are unemployed and the unemployment rate have increased overall since Labour took office in July 2024, but both have seen some month-to-month decreases.
claim: Unemployment has risen in every single month under Labour.

headline: Argos isn’t selling Apple Watch 9s for £3 to people who fill in a survey
rating_original: False. A spokesperson for Argos confirmed this isn’t a genuine offer from the retailer.
claim: Argos is selling Apple Watch 9s for £3 to people who fill in a survey.

headline: The government hasn’t announced ‘one of the harshest crackdowns’ UK drivers have ever seen
rating_original: False. A government spokesperson told Full Fact these claims are “untrue”. Videos on social media making this claim feature inauthentic audio with old footage of Sir Keir Starmer.
claim: From 1 October the government will introduce a crackdown on driving offences.

headline: Covid vaccine claims at the Reform UK conference: fact checked
rating_original: There is no credible evidence of a link between the Covid vaccines and cancer, and no evidence they were a factor in cancer cases within the Royal Family.
claim: A leading oncologist thinks it’s highly likely that the Covid vaccines have been a significant factor in the cancer of members of the Royal Family.

headline: Covid vaccine claims at the Reform UK conference: fact checked
rating_original: This is not correct, according to regulators and other experts. The Covid vaccines approved for use in the UK have met strict standards for safety and effectiveness.
claim: The Covid vaccine is unsafe.

headline: Covid vaccine claims at the Reform UK conference: fact checked
rating_original: This is potentially misleading. While the vaccine didn’t stop all infection or transmission in 2021, a UKHSA report at the time said the Covid vaccines then available were effective against infection and were preventing transmission.
claim: In the summer of 2021 we knew that the Covid vaccine wasn’t stopping infection or transmission.

headline: Covid vaccine claims at the Reform UK conference: fact checked
rating_original: We can’t say how accurate this claim is, as we have no way of directly verifying the exchange in 2021, but the chair of the BMA at the time has denied that he said this.
claim: The chair of the BMA told Dr Malhotra in December 2021 that most of his colleagues got their information on the Covid vaccine from the BBC.

headline: UK users do not have to provide ID to use VPNs
rating_original: This isn’t correct. The Online Safety Act means some websites, such as those publishing pornography, must carry out age checks, but VPN providers do not fall under these requirements. The screenshot of the article included with the post does not state that this is happening.
claim: All users of virtual private networks in the UK will now have to show ID to the providers.

headline: London Mayor is not building 40,000 new council homes ‘prioritised for Muslims’
rating_original: This isn’t true. There are 40,000 new council homes pledged to be built in London by the Mayor by the end of the decade, but these homes are not specifically for Muslims, or any particular demographic.
claim: The Mayor of London Sir Sadiq Khan has announced a new proposal to build 40,000 new council homes prioritised for Muslims under the Muslim housing plan and they will be built near mosques and halal shops.

headline: New mayor of Rotherham can speak English, contrary to online claims
rating_original: This is false. Mayor Rukhsana Ismail was born in Sheffield and can speak English fluently.
claim: Rotherham’s new mayor can’t speak English.

headline: Unsubstantiated claim that Donald Trump’s mother said he’d be a ‘disaster’ in politics reshared online
rating_original: There’s no evidence Mrs Trump ever said this.
claim: Donald Trump’s mother said her son was an idiot with “zero common sense” and “no social skills” and that she hoped he’d never get into politics as he’d be a “disaster”.

headline: How many children have been the victims of grooming gangs in the UK?
rating_original: This is an extrapolation that was shared by a peer in 2018, but we don’t know how it was calculated so it’s difficult to say how reliable it is. An inquiry in 2022 said “it is simply not possible to know the scale of child sexual exploitation by networks”.
claim: Over 250,000 children were sexually abused by grooming gangs in the first 18 years of this century.

headline: How many children have been the victims of grooming gangs in the UK?
rating_original: This is not a reliable estimate. It was made in 2015 by extrapolating figures from Rotherham, but the MP who produced it has since told us it is “completely unreliable”. An inquiry in 2022 said “it is simply not possible to know the scale of child sexual exploitation by networks”.
claim: One million children were sexually abused by grooming gangs.

headline: Video does not show recent footage of Israeli tanks moving to the Israel-Lebanon border
rating_original: This video is 11 months old and actually shows tanks being transported to Re’im, near the border with Gaza, after the 7 October attacks.
claim: A video shows tanks being moved north from Gaza to the Lebanese border in recent days.

headline: Turbulence video not from Singapore Airlines flight
rating_original: False. The video actually dates from 2019 and shows turbulence on a flight from Kosovo to Switzerland.
claim: A video shows “severe turbulence” on board a Singapore Airlines flight from London this week.

headline: Clip of missiles hitting ships is from video game Arma 3 (not the Red Sea)
rating_original: This is footage from the video game Arma 3 and does not depict a real-world incident.
claim: A video seemingly showing missiles hitting ships shows a naval battle in the Red Sea.

headline: False claims that Great Western Railway is giving away a year’s free travel for £1.69 spread online again
rating_original: False. The company has confirmed this is not a genuine offer.
claim: Great Western Railway is offering a gift card with a year’s free travel for £1.69.

headline: How many people have been intercepted while attempting to cross the Channel in small boats?
rating_original: This figure refers to the number of asylum applications made before 28 June 2022 which were outstanding as of 30 November 2022. The number of these cases which remain outstanding has since fallen to 74,436 as of 28 May 2023.
claim: There is a 92,000 legacy backlog.

headline: How many people have been intercepted while attempting to cross the Channel in small boats?
rating_original: Approximately 33,000 attempts by individuals to cross the English Channel by small boat were intercepted by French authorities in 2022, compared to around 23,000 in 2021—a roughly 43% increase. The percentage of attempts which were intercepted has fallen slightly, however.
claim: There’s been a 40% increase in the number of people that we are intercepting in the Channel.

headline: Man pictured with caravan has not gone missing in Grimsby
rating_original: This is false. Humberside Police have not issued a missing persons appeal for this man, and the picture used in the post has previously been used on social media to claim that a caravan has been stolen.
claim: A man called Martin Jones, who has dementia and is 79, has been reported missing in Grimsby.

headline: Government fails to back up PM’s claim that A&E patient flow is 'faster than ever'
rating_original: Neither Number 10 nor the Department of Health and Social Care have explained what figures Mr Sunak was referring to. NHS England data shows the volume of A&E attendances in December was the highest on record, but the proportion of patients waiting over four hours is also at a record high.
claim: The flow of patients through emergency care is faster than ever.

headline: Government fails to back up PM’s claim that A&E patient flow is 'faster than ever'
rating_original: It’s not clear exactly what this claim relates to. NHS England figures do show more patients have been discharged so far this winter than last, though we haven’t been able to find directly comparable figures beyond that. The proportion of patients declared medically fit who are discharged each day is lower than last winter.
claim: We are discharging people at a record rate out of hospitals.

headline: Do Treasury claims about a 'typical' first-time buyer’s savings add up?
rating_original: These figures are accurate in and of themselves. But in calculating the savings for this hypothetical buyer, the Treasury’s made a very specific set of assumptions.
claim: As a result of the government’s “Growth Plan”, a typical first-time buyer in London moving into a representative terraced house will save £11,250 on stamp duty and £1,050 on the household's energy bills—and if they earn £30,000, almost an additional £400 on tax. This is around £12,700 in total.

headline: The Coalition did not build more affordable homes in a year than Labour did in 13 years of government
rating_original: Incorrect. More than 550,000 affordable homes were completed during the period of Labour government. The most completed in any subsequent year of Conservative or coalition government has been about 66,000.
claim: The Conservative-led Coalition built more affordable homes in one year after 2010 than the Labour party did in 13 years in office.

headline: Wales and Scotland are getting money to fund a council tax rebate
rating_original: The Welsh and Scottish governments are receiving money from the UK government as a result of the council tax rebate scheme, but other areas of its estimated budget have been revised downwards as a result of England’s provisional budget for those areas being revised downwards too.
claim: There’s no extra money for Wales or Scotland to deliver the same council tax rebate scheme that was announced in England.
claim_author: Members of the Scottish and Welsh governments

headline: Why are media outlets reporting the Covid epidemic is escalating?
rating_original: At this point, new infections in the UK were falling. The total number of people with Covid-19, as opposed to newly diagnosed people, may have still been increasing.
claim: As of 2 November, case numbers are spiking.

headline: Why are media outlets reporting the Covid epidemic is escalating?
rating_original: At this point, new infections were falling, but the total number of people with Covid-19 may still have been increasing.
claim: As of 3 November, the UK’s coronavirus epidemic was escalating by the day.

headline: Viral impala picture is not a maternal sacrifice
rating_original: This is an image of an impala. The photographer says this is “a completely ridiculous fake story” and the image actually shows cheetah young practicing their hunting.
claim: Picture of a gazelle looking calm while being killed shows a mother sacrificing herself to allow her children to get away. Taking the photo led the photographer to fall into a depression.

headline: Post suggests American WW2 prisoners were British soldiers
rating_original: This is a famous photograph of two American civilians after the liberation of a Japanese POW camp in 1945.
claim: A photo of two emaciated men strongly implies they were British soldiers.

headline: We still don’t know if the UK does the most Covid-19 tests in Europe
rating_original: The UK appears to be testing fewer people than in Russia. But there isn’t enough data on this to determine for sure where the UK places, and the UK’s data isn’t particularly comparable with other countries.
claim: The UK is doing more Covid-19 tests than virtually any country in Europe.

headline: How poverty rates are cherry-picked to score political points
rating_original: The latest government figures show 14.5 million people (22% of the population) living in relative low income households after housing costs in the UK. In 2000/01 it was 13 million across Great Britain (23% of the population).
claim: There are roughly 14 million people living in relative poverty this year. In 2000, there were roughly 14 million people living in relative poverty.

headline: How poverty rates are cherry-picked to score political points
rating_original: Broadly correct. In 2010/11 the figure was 3.6 million (27% of children), and in 2018/19 it was 4.2 million (30% of children).However, if you measured from 2009/10, when the proportion was also 30%, there would be no change.
claim: In 2010-11, there were 3.5 million children living in relative poverty. Today, the figure after housing costs is 4.2 million.

headline: Change in LGBT+ hate crime levels not as simple as Dawn Butler suggests
rating_original: Incorrect. There are two sources of data on this type of hate crime. One estimates a 261% increase in hate crime on the basis of sexual orientation and transgender identity, and the other estimates a 40% decrease in hate crimes based on sexual orientation since around 2010. Neither measure is perfect.
claim: There has been a 400% increase in hate crime within the LGBT+ community.

headline: EU staff don’t lose their pensions for criticising the EU
rating_original: All three are ex-EU commissioners. None would lose their pension for criticising the EU.
claim: If Lord Kinnock, Lord Mandelson, or Lord Patten began to publicly criticise the EU, their pensions would be withdrawn.

headline: There is no EU police force being rolled out in the UK
rating_original: The photo is of Peruvian police officers. There is no current policy for an EU police force.
claim: A photo shows an EU police force which is coming to the UK.

headline: How many cyclists are killed each year?
rating_original: Correct for Britain. The 18,477 figure includes deaths, of which there were 102.
claim: In 2016, 18,477 cyclists were injured in road accidents, including 3,499 who were killed or seriously injured.

headline: How many cyclists are killed each year?
rating_original: Correct. Refers to figures for Britain in 2016.
claim: Of the almost 1,800 deaths that occur on our roads annually, around 450 are pedestrians in incidents where motor vehicles are involved.

headline: How many cyclists are killed each year?
rating_original: Roughly correct, for Britain.
claim: 0.5% of pedestrian deaths are people killed by people on a bike.

headline: Mental health: staff working in talking therapies
rating_original: One estimate says at least 2,850 more people worked in IAPT services (a flagship talking therapy programme for those with anxiety and depression) from August 2012 to April 2015. This does not include other NHS talking therapies.
claim: There are over 2,000 more people employed in talking therapies.

headline: Mental health: staff working in talking therapies
rating_original: One estimate says at least 2,850 more people worked in IAPT services (a flagship talking therapy programme for those with anxiety and depression) from August 2012 to April 2015. This does not include other NHS talking therapies.
claim: The increase in the number number of talking therapies staff is closer to 3,000 than 2,700.

headline: Has employment growth been driven by a rise in insecure, precarious work?
rating_original: That doesn’t seem to be the case for the UK jobs market overall. The picture for specific industries, regions and groups might be different and statistics will only ever give a limited insight into questions about job quality.
claim: At least a large part of growth in employment has been driven by an increase in insecure, precarious work.

headline: HS2: is it faster?
rating_original: Today a journey from Leeds to London takes around two hours. Using HS2 and going via Leeds, the journey could be around 25 minutes faster, though this doesn’t account for the time taken to change trains and board HS2, and compares current train times with the fastest possible estimates for HS2.
claim: It will take longer to get from Wakefield to London using HS2 than it does today.

headline: HS2: is it faster?
rating_original: Current government figures suggest that anything from 13 to 102 minutes could be taken off journey times from the north to London and Birmingham. This is comparing the current fastest times to the fastest times once HS2 is fully running in 2033.
claim: HS2 will only take a few minutes off the current journey time.

headline: School spending: up or down?
rating_original: Spending per pupil is set to fall in real terms, by 8%, according to the Institute for Fiscal Studies.
claim: Spending on schools is being cut.

headline: School spending: up or down?
rating_original: The cash amount has risen, but that doesn’t take into account inflation or rising pupil numbers.
claim: The schools budget has been increased over the past few years.

headline: The rising prison population
rating_original: It almost has, from 45,000 at the start of the 1990s to around 86,000 today in England and Wales. Prisons have been overcrowded almost constantly for the last two decades.
claim: The prison population has doubled in 25 years.

headline: Is the DWP reviewing a link between suicides and welfare reform?
rating_original: The DWP has carried out internal 'Peer Reviews' in 40 individual cases since February 2012 after the suicide or apparent suicide of a customer.
claim: The Department for Work and Pensions is or isn't carrying out a review of 60 suicides linked to benefits.
